properties.title: Bosch's Planned Closure Sparks Job Losses and Criticism
properties.summary: The Bosch Group's announcement of the impending closure of its Waschmaschinenfabrik in Nauen, Brandenburg, is set to result in 450 job losses, drawing sharp criticism from labor advocates. The article highlights the historical context of Bosch's restructuring efforts and the controversial support from IG Metall, which has been accused of prioritizing flexibility over job security. Author Andy Niklaus underscores the ongoing struggle against these job cuts, linking it to broader labor issues in the region.

properties.title: Bosch Faces Massive Fine Over Compliance Misunderstanding
properties.summary: A German trade compliance employee's confusion between the De Minimis-Rule and the expanded Foreign-Produced-Direct-Product-Rule has led to US authorities imposing a staggering civil fine of $36,184,680 against Bosch. The legal implications could have been even more severe, with potential penalties reaching twice the transaction value.

properties.title: Urgent Security Warning Issued for Bosch's BSH ELP Modules
properties.summary: INCIBE-CERT has issued an urgent security warning regarding three high-severity vulnerabilities in Bosch's BSH ELP modules, which are critical for industrial control systems. The vulnerabilities include a default insecure SSH configuration and outdated firmware, prompting Bosch to release corrected firmware within 72 hours of the notification.

properties.title: Job Cuts Loom at Bosch NüP1 Plant
properties.summary: The Robert Bosch Group's NüP1 plant in Nuremberg faces potential massive job cuts, as revealed in a recent works meeting attended by the works council and IG Metall. This alarming news has left the approximately 1,700 employees feeling unsettled, marking the second time in quick succession that such dire information has been communicated.

properties.title: Bosch Plans Job Cuts Amid Manufacturing Concerns
properties.summary: In a recent announcement, Bosch revealed plans to cut 13,000 jobs in Germany, raising alarms about the future of its manufacturing sites, particularly the Robert Bosch factory in Nuremberg. The company is under pressure to attract new products to ensure the viability of its Ruhr Bosch NuP1 site, as management refuses to extend the current site safeguard set to expire in 2026.

properties.title: Lawsuit Filed Against Bosch by LG Energy Solution
properties.summary: LG Energy Solution has initiated a lawsuit against Bosch, with representation from Quinn Emanuel and Dacus Law Firm. As the legal battle unfolds, public anger towards Bosch is escalating, although specific details regarding the lawsuit remain undisclosed.

properties.title: LG Energy Solution Files Patent Infringement Lawsuit Against Robert Bosch GmbH
properties.summary: LG Energy Solution has initiated a patent infringement lawsuit in Texas against Robert Bosch GmbH, accusing the company of unlawfully using its proprietary secondary cylindrical battery technology. This legal action highlights the intensifying competition in the battery industry, particularly as advancements in technology become increasingly critical for electric vehicles and consumer electronics.

properties.title: D1R Ransomware Group Claims Hack of Bosch via Synopsys
properties.summary: A new ransomware group named D1R has claimed to have hacked Bosch Group, alleging access to sensitive intellectual property through a vulnerability in Synopsys' systems. While D1R has threatened to leak proprietary hardware design files unless a ransom is paid, Synopsys has stated that it found no evidence of a data breach, raising questions about the authenticity of the hackers' claims.

properties.title: Bosch Group Announces Major Job Cuts Amid Automotive Crisis
properties.summary: In a significant move, Bosch Group plans to cut up to 22,000 jobs in its automotive division, highlighting the severe impact of the ongoing crisis in the German automotive industry. This decision marks the largest reduction among suppliers, reflecting the challenges posed by falling demand and the shift towards electric mobility.

properties.title: Bosch Group Restructuring Sparks Urgent Calls for Dialogue
properties.summary: In light of significant financial losses, Bosch Group has announced the cessation of operations in several locations, prompting a drastic reduction in workforce. The chief of Bosch Betriebsrat is now advocating for urgent discussions among employers, unions, and political leaders to address the implications of these layoffs and to seek solutions that protect workers and support affected communities.

properties.title: Bosch to Close Major Engineering Center in Bulgaria, Impacting 670 Jobs
properties.summary: Bosch has announced the closure of its Engineering Center in Sofia, Bulgaria, which is set to result in the loss of approximately 670 jobs by mid-2027. This decision is part of a global restructuring strategy aimed at addressing significant shifts in the automotive sector, including rising costs and intensified competition.

properties.title: Bosch Automotive Restructuring Leads to Job Transfers in Romania
properties.summary: In 2025, Bosch Automotive reported a significant restructuring that resulted in a 37% reduction in its workforce in Romania, equating to 970 jobs. However, the company clarified that these were not layoffs but rather a transfer of employees to Bosch Rexroth, which experienced a substantial increase in its workforce during the same period.

properties.title: Nationwide Industrial Strike Announced
properties.summary: A 2-hour work stoppage is set to take place at the Belgian locations of ASML, DAF Trucks, Bosch, and Nedri Spanstaal this Friday. This strike is part of the FNV's intensified campaign against the Dutch government's proposed austerity measures, which have faced significant backlash from labor unions.

properties.title: Bosch Group Avoids Prosecution After Self-Reporting Sanction Violations
properties.summary: The Bosch Group has been cleared of prosecution by the DOJ after it voluntarily disclosed its transactions with a sanctioned Chinese company. This decision underscores the importance of self-reporting and cooperation in compliance with international sanctions and national security laws.

properties.title: Bosch's Expansion Plans in Limbo Amid Financial Struggles
properties.summary: Despite initial agreements for expansion, Bosch's plans for its research center in Renningen-Malmsheim remain uncertain due to recent financial difficulties and job cuts. Meanwhile, the state of Baden-Württemberg and the federal government are moving forward with preparations for a new parachute drop zone for the KSK, indicating a shift in focus away from Bosch's expansion.

properties.title: Bosch Group Announces Leadership Change Amid Restructuring
properties.summary: Stefan Hartung has announced his resignation as CEO of Bosch Group, effective July 1, to pursue new social and entrepreneurial endeavors. His departure comes as the company faces significant challenges, including a major restructuring plan that will cut 18,500 jobs to improve competitiveness in a struggling automotive market. Christian Fischer, currently the chief of Bosch's consumer goods division, will take over as CEO.

properties.title: Bosch Group Settles for $36 Million Over Unauthorized Exports to Huawei
properties.summary: Bosch Group has agreed to pay a $36 million settlement to the U.S. government for exporting over $70 million worth of sensor products and software to Huawei without the necessary licenses. This settlement follows Bosch's self-disclosure of the violations, which occurred more than 100 times between 2020 and 2024, and the Justice Department has opted not to prosecute the company as a result of its cooperation.

properties.title: Bosch CEO Warns of Supply Chain Risks Amid Middle East Conflict
properties.summary: In light of the ongoing Middle East conflict, Bosch CEO Stefan Hartung has raised concerns about potential supply chain disruptions, particularly regarding the availability of critical raw materials like helium for semiconductors. Despite these emerging risks, Bosch remains optimistic about achieving its 2026 financial targets, although it plans to continue job cuts in its automotive sector.

properties.title: Bosch Factory Sale Sparks Job Security Negotiations
properties.summary: The Bosch factory in Vendôme, currently up for sale, has concluded a labor strike that began on May 28. Following the strike, negotiations are now underway between workers' representatives and local management to secure job guarantees amid concerns over the future of the plant.

properties.title: New Antitrust Lawsuit Filed Against HVAC Manufacturers
properties.summary: A new civil antitrust lawsuit has been filed in the Eastern District of Michigan, targeting Robert Bosch LLC and other major HVAC manufacturers for alleged price-fixing practices. The lawsuit claims that these companies conspired to stabilize and raise prices of HVAC equipment since January 2020, significantly impacting consumers and businesses during the COVID-19 pandemic.

properties.title: Bosch Vendôme Plant Strike Enters Second Week Amid Job Security Fears

The strike has drawn attention from local politicians, who are calling for government action and ecological planning to support reindustrialization efforts in France.

properties.title: Lawsuit Dismissed in Bosch Group Data Breach Case

properties.title: Bosch Boosts Investment in Portugal's Electric Mobility and Heat Pump Sectors
